$comment: Allowlist for scripts/check-finding-regression-pins.mjs (W2-CI-001). Each entry is an F-id that appears in source files but has no corresponding test pin, AND has a deliberate justification. The parser is intentionally permissive — it cannot distinguish 'this comment IS a fix pin' from 'this comment MENTIONS the id' (see parse-regression-pins.js JSDoc 'permissive limitation'). Cross-references in source comments are the most common legitimate orphan; this allowlist captures them so the always-on CI gate stays green without forcing test pins for prose mentions. Adding an entry: F-id key, value is an object with at least { reason, file }. Entries should be revisited each release — if the source reference goes away, drop the allowlist entry.

F-693631-010.reason: Cross-reference in scripts/build.mjs comment naming the drift class — not a fix-site pin, the pin lives in packages/dogfood-swarm where the AUDIT_PHASES enum is enforced.

F-742440-002.reason: Cross-reference in packages/dogfood-swarm/commands/persist.js comment pointing readers at persist-results.js for the canonical pattern. Test coverage lives with the canonical pattern.

F-742440-012.reason: Cross-reference in packages/dogfood-swarm/db/schema.js naming a wave-1 sibling. Test coverage lives with the sibling fix in wave-1.

F-COORD-004.reason: Cross-reference in .github/workflows/ci.yml naming the doc-drift CLASS (error code / status enum / legacy path added without its sibling doc entry) that scripts/check-doc-drift.mjs catches generically via scripts/doc-drift-patterns.json. There is no single fix-site to pin: the check is config-driven (error-codes, statuses, and further entries in doc-drift-patterns.json), and each entry is exercised by scripts/check-doc-drift.test.mjs — including the non-vacuity 'error-codes META' test that strips an enforced code from the handbook and asserts drift fires. Real coverage lives there, not at this citation.

F-5b0996e4.reason: Doc-only correction in packages/dogfood-swarm/commands/dispatch.js's dispatch() header: fixes a prior version of the SAME header that wrongly claimed both worktree creation and prompt-file writes were 'EXPLICITLY outside the tx'. Worktree creation running INSIDE db.transaction() (so a thrown IsolationError rolls back all DB writes while any already-created worktree survives as an FS orphan) is exactly what packages/dogfood-swarm/amend2-d3b-002-dispatch-tx.test.js's D3B-002 suite exercises ('mid-loop failure rolls back ALL DB writes' — triggered via --isolate with no .git, i.e. IsolationError propagating out of the tx). That coverage predates and is independent of this id; the fix here is the corrected prose, not new behavior.

F-W1-CI-001.reason: Cross-reference in .github/workflows/pages.yml naming the historical id for the pa11y job-permission-isolation restructure — the same restructure the file elsewhere attributes to F-a52776d5 (both appear independently in prose, not dual-labeled at one site). Real behavioral coverage is scripts/stageC-check-pages-a11y-isolation.test.mjs's F-a52776d5/F-32c517c4 tests, which assert the a11y job is dedicated with `permissions: {}` and that pa11y does NOT run inside the elevated deploy job — the exact property this citation describes.

F-e241fa61.reason: Doc-only correction in packages/dogfood-swarm/commands/redrive.js's AGENT_ELIGIBLE_SOURCES comment, clarifying that a WAVE-level 'failed' status (unlike an agent-level 'failed') is BLOCKED and needs the override path. The behavior itself — a failed wave redriven only via override — is exercised by packages/dogfood-swarm/redrive.test.js's 'failed wave is redriven via override path (BLOCKED source)' test (describe block 'redrive — wave-level transition paths'), which predates and is independent of this id.
